source: made up: person having a terrible day with poor sleep and a dead car battery who cancels half the plan and asks the app to make it manageable
persona: Victor, a freelance insurance claims adjuster who had an awful night of insomnia after his upstairs neighbor's smoke detector chirped until 04:00. Texts in exhausted, defeated sentences; when his car won't start at lunchtime, he hits his limit and asks the app to ruthlessly triage his afternoon down to bare survival mode.
situation: Tuesday morning waking at 08:45 after barely four hours of sleep, having slept through his 07:00 alarm. Supposed to write three claim reports, drive to an afternoon site inspection, go to the bank and Costco, work out, and cook dinner.
life: 08:50 Wake up in a panic after sleeping through the 07:00 alarm because the upstairs neighbor's smoke alarm chirped all night. Text the app: terrible night of sleep, just woke up at 08:45. I'm exhausted. Help me salvage today: quick coffee & toast now, write the 3 desktop claim reports 09:30–12:00, grab lunch and drive to the 13:30 Oak St roof inspection, hit Costco and the bank on the way back at 15:00, finish admin emails until 16:30, and cook stir-fry tonight.
08:55 Drop the morning workout immediately—remind the app there is zero chance I'm lifting weights on 4 hours of sleep.
09:00 Drink two cups of black coffee and eat toast while staring bleary-eyed at laptop until 09:30.
09:32 Report coffee and toast done. Starting the 3 desktop claim reports now.
09:35 Grind through only 2 of the 3 desktop claim reports because your brain is moving through molasses, finishing the second one at 12:15.
12:18 Text the app: only got 2 of the 3 claim reports done, my head is pounding. Eating a quick sandwich now and walking out to the car at 12:45 to drive to the 13:30 Oak St inspection.
12:20 Eat a turkey sandwich, grab clipboard and camera, and go out to the driveway at 12:45—turn the key and the car battery is completely dead (left the dome light on last night).

12:55 Call AAA for a jump/battery test and call the Oak St homeowner to move the roof inspection to Thursday morning. Text the app at 13:05: my car battery is completely dead in the driveway. Called AAA (coming between 13:30 and 15:00) and moved the Oak St inspection to Thursday. Today is officially cursed. Please cancel Costco, cancel the bank run, cancel cooking stir-fry—just help me make the rest of this day manageable so I don't lose my mind.

13:10 Agree to the stripped-down survival plan: wait for AAA and finish that 3rd desktop claim report so today isn't a total write-off, let AAA replace/jump the battery, take a 45-minute afternoon nap once the car is dealt with, order pho delivery for dinner, and go to bed at 21:30.
13:15 Sit on the front porch steps with laptop so you can see the tow truck, and finish writing the 3rd desktop claim report by 14:10.
14:12 AAA battery truck arrives; tech tests the 6-year-old battery (dead cell) and installs a new battery right in the driveway, finishing at 14:50.
14:55 Text the app: 3rd claim report is submitted AND the AAA tech put a brand-new battery in my car! Logging off work early—going to close the blinds and take a 1-hour nap right now (15:00–16:00).
15:00 Sleep deeply in a dark bedroom until 16:15.

16:20 Wake up from nap feeling slightly less miserable. Text the app: nap done. Taking a warm shower and then doing literally nothing except answering two quick client emails so my inbox doesn't explode tomorrow.
16:25 Take a warm shower and send two status emails until 17:15.
17:20 Report shower and emails done. Order beef pho and spring rolls on DoorDash at 18:00, eat on the couch at 18:45, and go to sleep early at 21:30.
constraints: Running on 4 hours of sleep: cannot do workouts or heavy batch errands.
Dead car battery in the driveway prevents driving to the 13:30 site inspection, Costco, or the bank, and requires waiting at home for the AAA battery truck.
When overwhelmed by compounding mishaps, non-essential errands and cooking must be dropped in favor of rest and takeout.
